# Visualization brief

Specification: Science Ladder visualization v1

Complete this file as `visualization/README.md` in the challenge repository. Replace
prompts with concrete answers. Use `needs_work` when essential facts or implementation
are missing; do not invent a successful check.

## Learning goal

What should a curious reader understand in one minute? Which scientific object,
frontier obstacle and meaningful improvement does this figure explain?

## Figure and metric

Describe the main figure and the exact meaning of each visual encoding. Name the
manifest metric and constraints. Explain the relationship between visible changes,
verified progress, scientific significance and claims the figure cannot support.

## Reference and provenance

Name the exact public reference artifact, actual byte digest, primary sources and
reproduction/export commands. Describe the `reference.json` data shape, units,
rounding, tolerances, approximation and any reduced illustration. State how it is
compared against the frozen checker. Document third-party rights and attribution.

## Controls

For each control: label, initial value, allowed range, effect, learning purpose,
keyboard/touch operation and context fields it updates. Explain Reset reference.
For a static figure, explain why interaction adds no useful scientific understanding.

## Implementation

Give local build/preview commands, file structure, dependency locks, rendering
choice, data bounds and any worker/precomputation. Include a text fallback.
Describe actual platform integration and remaining work separately from the preview.

## Learning-guide state

Document every field of `context.schema.json`, its meaning/unit/limits and an example
snapshot. Implement `window.scienceLadderVisualization.getContext()` in the preview.
Keep the snapshot below 8 KiB and distinguish reference, local edits and published
verified artifacts. No trusted status can originate from this browser state.

## Accessibility and performance

Describe keyboard/touch access, labels, non-color encodings, text/table equivalent,
reduced motion, 200% zoom, 390/1440 px layouts, data limits, responsive controls and
scroll chaining. State the environment and actual measurements for performance claims.

## Checks and limitations

Link `checks.md` with numerical comparisons, screenshots, actual browser checks,
invalid-data behavior and unresolved issues. State what the visualization does not
measure or prove. A screenshot or local score is not an official verification receipt.
